PROVISIONAL INFERENCE, NOT AN AAT-SPECIFIC VERIFIED INTERNATIONAL RATE. Australia Post's official Post Charges guide (effective 1 September 2026) p. 2 identifies Australian Antarctic Territory as Tasmania (TAS) 7151 for postal charging and explicitly states domestic ordinary-letter charges apply to mail to/from the territory within Australia: small regular letter 1.85 AUD (p. 4, up to 250 g). The same guide p. 31 lists International Economy Air Small Letter up to 250 g to Germany (Zone 4, UK & Europe) at 4.70 AUD. The PDF does NOT explicitly confirm that letters lodged at Antarctic stations for overseas delivery are charged that international rate. The earlier collector-supplied 4.00 AUD was unsupported. The guide also cautions that using domestic stamps to frank international mail may require 10% additional postage for GST (p. 30); confirm station-specific acceptance and stamp treatment before franking. Australian Antarctic Division confirms station postmasters may cancel letters for Australia Post and recommends a prepaid domestic return envelope for collector covers (https://www.antarctica.gov.au/news/stations/casey/2024/31-may/).

check.detail: Australia Post official guide confirms AAT domestic treatment and international Australia Zone 4 rate, but does not verify that 4.70 AUD applies directly to AAT-origin overseas station mail; PDF manual review only.

rates.notes: PROVISIONAL TRANSFER OF GUERNSEY RATE, NOT A SARK-SPECIFIC VERIFIED RATE. Guernsey Post expressly states that Sark operates under Guernsey postal administration and Sark issued its first official postage stamps in Aug–Sep 2025. Guernsey Post's official 2026 'Sending Letters' tariff (1 April 2026) shows ordinary standard Europe Letter up to 100 g at £2.96. The same rate likely applies to ordinary Sark-origin letters to Germany under the shared postal network; however, no source explicitly confirmed this precise tariff for a letter lodged on Sark and franked with Sark stamps. Confirm with Guernsey Post's philatelic bureau or Sark Post Office before preparing a stamped collector cover. Sark and Alderney have distinct stamp issues but are not independent tariff systems.
